title: Pulling pots
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The end of the season. The uncle pulls his pots with Gully and the strip watches from the dock. Wood is told to draw or hold the line; he can't do both.

panels.composition: The boat launch, October, gray chop. The UNCLE's skiff at the dock, GULLY hauling a crab pot over the gunwale, the uncle at the tiller. WOOD on the dock with the pad.

image.prompt: an old man at a skiff's tiller and a stocky teenager hauling a crab pot over the gunwale at a small boat launch in gray chop, a young man on the dock with a drawing pad, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The uncle, flat-faced, rain hood up.

balloons.text: Draw or hold the line. Not both.

image.prompt: a weathered old man in a rain hood at a boat's tiller speaking flatly, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood's hands: the pad in one, the wet line in the other. Both.

image.prompt: close on a young man's hands, one holding a drawing pad and one holding a wet rope, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The pot coming over. Water everywhere. The pad soaked. The drawing on it: a pot, half done, running. Gully laughing without sound.

image.prompt: a crab pot coming over a gunwale in a spray of water soaking a drawing pad, a teenager laughing silently, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: The uncle's rule. The pad is soaked; the drawing runs.
